hooks.text: A giant black hole hurled a star out of our galaxy.
Which gravity monster has the power to banish stars from our galaxy?
One star is fleeing our galaxy at four million miles per hour.

title: The Star Escaping Our Galaxy at 4 Million MPH
description: Discover S5-HVS1, a hypervelocity star flung by Sagittarius A* that is currently fleeing the Milky Way forever.

beats.text: A giant black hole hurled a star out of our galaxy.
beats.visual: artist concept of a hypervelocity star being ejected by a black hole NASA, 2019
queries: black hole binary star tidal disruption illustration NASA

beats.text: Astronomers tracked this stellar runaway, known as S5-HVS1, roughly 29,000 light-years away from Earth.
Sergey [Koposov](/kˈOpˈʌsˈɑf/) and a team of researchers used Gaia spacecraft data to trace its direct path.
The star travels at an extraordinary velocity of approximately 1,755 kilometers per second.
beats.visual: Milky Way structure diagram with trajectory of escaping star, 2019
queries: Milky Way Galaxy spiral arms diagram

beats.text: This speed is more than triple what is required to break free from our home galaxy.
beats.visual: diagram of escape velocity from the Milky Way, 2019

beats.text: It was kicked out of the galactic center approximately five million years ago.
beats.visual: artist concept of Milky Way galactic center, 2015

beats.text: Our central black hole, Sagittarius A*, captured its partner star and violently slung this one away.
beats.visual: Chandra X-ray image of Sagittarius A* at the galactic center, 2019

beats.text: Now, this lonely outcast is fleeing the Milky Way at nearly four million miles per hour.
beats.visual: artist concept of a lone star wandering in intergalactic space, 2019
